title: Embedding ingress packet coordinator and quantile-driven prefill smoothing
creator: Alyssa Park
description: Goal: Reduce end-to-end p99/p995 latency for the embeddings endpoint across multi-tenant hosts by reducing packetization overhead and stabilizing prefill-induced stragglers. Background: Recent heatmaps show recurring long tails when small requests collide with large multi-tenant bursts and when prefill/warmup tasks evict active KV cache entries. Prior approaches (coalescing, larger microbatches) lowered mean cost but introduced variable latency for latency-sensitive tenants. This ticket implements a lightweight Packet Coordinator in the ingress layer plus a quantile-driven prefill smoothing policy that adapts prefill aggressiveness based on tenant latency CDFs.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for 95th percentile of tenants reduced by >= 20% on benchmark traffic
p995 tail improved by >= 15% without increasing mean token cost by > 5%
no customer-visible regression on throughput or error-rate in canary (1% traffic) over 48h
automated metric dashboards (per-tenant p50/p90/p99) added and alerting configured
plan: Landing design doc + sequence diagram for Packet Coordinator and prefill smoothing (Week 1)
Implement Packet Coordinator: ingress-level packetization that groups short requests into tenant-cohorts using time-window and packet-size heuristics (Week 2)
Implement Quantile Prefill Smoothing: keep a rolling CDF of per-tenant latency and throttle prefill/eviction aggressiveness based on quantile targets (Week 2-3)
Integrate tenant-aware slot sizing: dynamic slot budgets per-tenant to reduce cross-tenant interference (Week 3)
Run controlled canary (1% traffic) for 48h, collect histograms and allocation traces (Week 4)
Rollout to 10% then 50% with rollback runbooks if regression observed (Week 5)
Postmortem and tuning: adjust thresholds and eviction sensitivity based on observed tails (Week 6)
metrics: median and tail KV cache hit rate per-tenant
per-request token cost and aggregate cost delta versus baseline
ingress batching efficiency (requests per packet, latency added by packetization)
request error rate and timeout counts
CPU/GPU utilization and queue occupancy on targeted hosts
experiments: A/B1: Baseline vs packet coordinator with fixed 5ms window and max packet 8 — measure added latency vs batching efficiency
A/B2: Packet coordinator + cohorting by tenant fingerprint (short vs long request cohorts) vs time-only batching
A/B3: Prefill smoothing: aggressive prefill (baseline) vs quantile-based throttle targeting p95<150ms
A/B4: Dynamic slot sizing enabled vs disabled with identical workload generator and tenant mixes
Stress test: synthetic burst mix with 10x short requests and 1x heavy embed requests run for 2h to surface eviction/regression modes
decisions: Use a soft time-window packetization default (5ms) that can be overridden per-tenant by policy
Maintain a lightweight in-ingress bidder (no persistent DB) — cohort state lives in ephemeral host memory and rehydrates on restart
Prefill smoothing will use exponentially-weighted CDF estimates (EWMA of quantiles) to avoid noisy quantile jumps
Do not change kernel-level scheduling in this ticket; kernel hints will be a follow-up once ingress shaping proves stable
risks: Packetization could add headroom to median latency for single-request tenants if misconfigured
Ephemeral cohort state increases complexity during host failover; may need a reconciliation pass
Quantile estimation could be noisy for low-volume tenants leading to oscillation — mitigation is EWMA smoothing and minimum sample counts
Interplay with existing autoscaler: dynamic slot sizing might create feedback loops with burst autoscaling thresholds
